notes: A decision is scanned when the mover has both a safe play (0 hitting rolls for the opponent) and an unsafe play (12 or more hitting rolls), there is contact, and there are more than 2 legal plays. Invalid answers (fallback) are skipped.
Gap = 2-ply cubeless equity of the best unsafe play minus that of the best safe play (GNU Backgammon). Risk wins: gap of +0.04 or more. Safety wins: gap of -0.04 or less. Both are 'flagged'.

3-ply stability check (it replaced rollouts for the leagues): a flagged decision is kept only if the gap is 0.04 or more at both 2-ply and 3-ply, has the same sign at both, and the two gaps differ by 0.02 or less. It is a stability signal, not a rollout.
Kept: 25,199 of 32,840 flagged decisions (7,997 Risk wins, 17,202 Safety wins).
The method was written down and committed before any computation; the 3-ply rule was committed before any 3-ply value was computed.

sections.title: Checks on the scan

notes: Sample: 200 kept positions drawn with a fixed seed, 100 Risk wins and 100 Safety wins, about a third per gap band; Bray position excluded. Oversample: 30 back-game and 30 prime-vs-prime kept positions not in the 200 (fixed seed), reported separately and not used in Part 2.

Settings: GNU Backgammon 1.08.003, 1,296 games per play, variance reduction, quasi-random dice, same seed for both plays, no truncation, cubeless money play with gammons and backgammons counted (1/2/3 points), Jacoby off, 2-ply checker play (cubeless, prune, no noise). Each play is rolled out from the position after it, opponent on roll.
Confirmed = same direction as the scan, rollout gap 0.04 or more, and more than 3 standard errors of the gap. The rule, the settings and the oversample were committed before the first rollout.

189 of 200 confirmed (94.5%): 93 of 100 Risk wins, 96 of 100 Safety wins. No position flipped; all 11 misses are in the 0.04-0.08 band with a smaller gap in the same direction. Back game 39 of 40, prime-vs-prime 40 of 40 (sample and oversample together); most of those are large-gap Safety wins already kept by the 3-ply check, so this says nothing about the positions the check dropped.

sections.title: Rollout check of a 200-position sample

notes: Preliminary / partial. Two or four plays shown, not league play.

Positions: the 189 rollout-confirmed sample positions (93 Risk wins, 96 Safety wins). Each question is its own request with no shared context. Not paired across models beyond these shared items, and the league comparison is unpaired (the models played in different leagues on different positions).

Q1: best safe vs best unsafe play, 'Which play is better?'; half the right answers are A (fixed seed). Q2 (board only, 60 items where exactly one option is true of the unsafe play B and not of the safe play A): what does play B do that play A does not; random baseline 25%. Q3: 3 or 4 plays (best safe, best unsafe, best in-between if any, one clear blunder at least 0.10 below the others at 3-ply if any) and their 3-ply values (2 decimals, labelled W-Z); chat models match each value to a play (each play once), decision models get one question per value.
Two versions: with numbers (the league prompt with the computed consequences of each play) and board only (notation only, no pip count or other computed number).

Models at league settings; temperature not sent (provider default) for all. Decision models: the top-probability option is the answer; an exact tie at the top is no answer. Q3 scoring: only pairs 0.04 or more apart at 3-ply; a decision model that puts two values on one play gets the pairs of that play wrong; a chat answer that is not one-to-one counts every pair wrong.

GPT-6.1 Sol (high): pending, not collected (its subscription was busy with other queued jobs). Its rows are NA, never 0%. This is separate from the Codex effort sweep, whose GPT-6.1 Sol (max) row is a different run.

Q3 random baselines were added AFTER the first score output: first score 2026-10-30T06:25:29.387Z, baseline edit 2026-10-30T06:25:46.496Z, baseline output 2026-10-30T06:25:50.444Z. Not pre-registered and not exact: a simulation with seed 2026103005, 200 draws per item (4000 // 20), rounded to whole percent. Scoring was not changed.
The cross-table's 'doesn't know the game' uses the board-only Q2 answer for both versions (Q2 was asked board only).

Denominators: expected = items sent per model; recorded = answer rows stored; usable = recorded minus rows with a request error, invalid answers and exact ties. 'Item-level flags' for decision models count Q3 items (position and version) where two values went to one play, not pairs and not failed requests. Answer-row error counts are rows whose request failed after retries, not attempts.
Cost: hosted decision models at list price (the cash cap was $3; the stored list-price total is about $0.59); Claude Sonnet 5.5 (high) on a subscription, shown as API-equivalent, not money paid.
